_doc: Revert-verify mutants for ticket 534a7a46, req 675cb0ab-b73d-4736-934d-6094e792af5d — SUBJECT: packages/core/src/services/GroundingExecutor.ts. Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout. Guards enumerated from `git diff -U0` (integration-test-revert-verify §A8). ⛤ ME3 is the gate's own mutant, required by the ORCH plan-gate: the ticket's property_set change is reached ONLY when scalarTypingForRange(range) !== undefined, and without that gate the shape guards inside needsYamlQuoting would quote a deliberate flow array on its leading `[` and break multi-class convert — so ME3 must redden K13/K14 (the verbatim axes) and leave the typing axes green. ⛔ NAMED, not mutated (§A35): the iriToObsidianName call in executePropertySet is DEFENSIVE — CommandResolver.getObsidianName (CommandResolver.ts:3696) already puts targetProperty in prefix__Name form with the same inverse, so on every resolver-driven path iriToObsidianName returns null and the fallback runs; no axis can distinguish the two, and an axis on the IRI form would specify an input production cannot produce (§A37). Probed 2026-09-20: a hand-built grounding with the IRI form does resolve the range, but its write key degrades to the raw IRI — a pre-existing defect of that unreachable shape, raised separately rather than adopted as this requirement's contract.

ME1_port_not_stored._note: Drops the wiring entirely: every typing axis falls back to the shape rule. K10/K11 (controls) and K13/K14 (verbatim) must stay green — they assert the pre-ticket shape, which is what this mutant restores. ⛤ K18 was added to `expect` on 2026-10-02 (issue #4518) only AFTER reading why it reddens, not to silence the driver (§A44): ticket afb25c43 introduced K18 — the ARRAY emission point — AFTER these expectations were measured, and with the port unwired the array items fall back to the same shape rule as the scalar, so each canonical negative integer is quoted on its leading `-`. K19 is K18's port-absent control and asserts exactly that quoted form, so it stays green. ⛤ K20 (added here) also stays green: with `this.declaredRanges` undefined the property_set gate is never entered and the value is written verbatim, which for `true` is the same bare `true` the fixed code emits — the same 'green for an independent reason' shape K12 had on the first run. ⛤ K12 was ABSENT from the measured red set on the first run, and that was a real finding about the AXIS, not about this mutant: K12 then asserted a canonical integer under xsd:integer, and property_set writes an untyped value VERBATIM, so both outcomes were the bare `-1003912427125`. The axis was green for an independent reason. K12 now uses xsd:string / `42`, where bare and quoted differ.

ME2_create_instance_does_not_read_the_po._note: ⛤ K18 added to `expect` 2026-10-02 (issue #4518) with its reason read first, not dictated by the driver (§A44): this mutant kills the create_instance READ, and K18 — introduced later by ticket afb25c43 — IS a create_instance axis (the array emission point), so an empty map makes every item fall back to the shape rule and be quoted. K12 stays green because property_set keeps its own read, and K20 (property_set) likewise. Type-PRESERVING (§A36): the port is still consulted for PRESENCE, so `declaredRanges` keeps its `ReadonlyMap | undefined` type and the lookup below still type-checks — it just never asks the port for anything. The first form assigned a bare `undefined`, which narrowed the variable to `undefined` and broke `.get` at the call site (TS2339 → BROKEN, no verdict).

ME5_string_scalar_flag_forced_on_under_a._note: ⛔ THIS MUTANT'S PREVIOUS `expect: []` WAS WRONG, and the correction is shown rather than silently applied (issue #4518). The retracted claim read: «NO DISTINGUISHING INPUT on this axis set … it would matter only for a property that is BOTH in STRING_SCALAR_PROPERTIES and carries a numeric range». It is inverted: forcing the flag to `true` is a literal no-op for a property that IS in STRING_SCALAR_PROPERTIES (there `isStringScalarProperty` is already `true`), so the mutation can only differ where the property is NOT in the set. ⛤ MEASURED on this tree 2026-10-02 (serializeYamlScalar(value, false|true, range), 12 inputs): `true`/`false` under xsd:string → bare vs quoted; `010` / `1_000` / `0x1F` / `08` / `12345678901234567890` under xsd:integer → bare vs quoted; `yes` under xsd:boolean → bare vs quoted. Only the CANONICAL lexical forms (`42`, `-1003912427125`, `1.5`) are indistinguishable, because for those the numeric branch returns before the quoteAmbiguousScalars check — which is the part of the retracted claim that was true, and the part that made the false conclusion look measured. ⇒ the mutation is faithful and load-bearing; what was missing was an AXIS (integration-test-revert-verify §A130), so K20 was added rather than this mutant repointed or removed (the issue's outcome 2 as literally worded). K20 pins `true` under an xsd:string range on a property outside STRING_SCALAR_PROPERTIES staying BARE — the carve-out `!CANONICAL_YAML_BOOLEAN` in needsYamlQuoting, with 233 live carriers in `exoas-flow` (measured 2026-09-19, yamlScalar.ts), so the input is production-real, not invented for the mutant.
